pattern.summary: 8 questions, attempt any 5, each carries 20 marks. All theory; Q8 is always 'short notes on any two of four'. Examiners ask for examples in almost every question.

choosing: The same questions repeat almost word for word: buyer behaviour factors, buying motives, sales reports, motivating salespeople, objection handling and closing techniques.
Q8 (any two short notes of four) is a safe pick — sales manual, prospecting and ethics come up again and again.
Almost every question says 'with examples' — give one Indian example (a product you know) in every point.

topics.name: Sales Reports, Documents & Sales Manual
topics.summary: Sales reports (objectives, features, types), documents salespeople prepare, sales manual, order book.
points: Sales report: a written account of a salesperson's activities and results for a period.
Objectives: record performance, give market feedback (competitors, prices, complaints), help planning and control, basis for evaluation and pay.
Features of a good report: accurate, timely, brief and clear, complete, standard format, factual, action-oriented.
Types: daily call report, weekly/monthly work report, expense report, new-customer report, lost-sale report, complaint report, market/competitor report.
Documents: sales manual, order book/order form, route plan, price list, product catalogue, quotation, invoice, customer records.

Sales manual: a handbook of company policies, product details, selling methods and procedures. Contents: company history and policies, product information, prices and terms, selling techniques, handling objections, reporting procedures. Benefits: uniform approach, training aid, confidence, saves supervisors' time.
Order book: records orders taken with customer details, quantity, price and delivery terms.
topics.frame: Meaning → objectives or contents as headed points → a sample format (columns of a call report) → benefits → conclusion.

topics.name: Sales Presentation, Demonstration & Objections
topics.summary: Presentation and demonstration steps and strategies, and handling objections.
points: Presentation: telling the prospect how the product meets their needs; demonstration: showing it in action.
Steps: prepare (know the prospect and product) → approach and gain attention → identify needs → present benefits (features → advantages → benefits) → demonstrate → handle objections → move to close.
Strategies/methods: stimulus–response (canned), formula (AIDA — attention, interest, desire, action), need-satisfaction, problem-solution, consultative.
Good demonstration: let the prospect handle the product, show the key benefit, keep it short, use testimonials.
Objections: price, product, company, timing ('I'll think about it'), need.

Handling techniques: listen fully, 'yes… but', direct denial (for wrong facts), boomerang (turn the objection into a reason to buy), compensation (admit and offset), question method, third-party proof, postpone.
topics.frame: Meaning → steps or strategies as headed points, each with one product example → conclusion.
mistakes: Arguing with the prospect is itself a listed mistake — mention 'never argue' when writing on objections.

topics.name: Motivating & Paying Salespeople
topics.summary: Role of motivation, Maslow's theory for salespeople, financial and non-financial techniques, compensation plans.
points: Salespeople work alone, face rejection and irregular results — so motivation matters more than in most jobs.

Maslow applied to salespeople: physiological (fair salary), safety (job security, insurance), social (team meetings, belonging), esteem (recognition, awards, titles), self-actualisation (challenging targets, promotion).
Financial techniques: salary, commission, bonus, incentives, contests with cash prizes, profit sharing, fringe benefits.
Non-financial: recognition, praise, job enrichment, training, promotion, participation in goal setting, sales meetings, conventions.
Compensation plans: straight salary (security, less push), straight commission (strong push, insecure), combination (salary + commission/bonus — most common), plus expense allowances.
topics.frame: Meaning → Maslow pyramid adapted to salespeople → financial vs non-financial table → conclusion.

topics.name: Buying Motives
topics.summary: Meaning, types and application of buying motives in personal selling.
points: Buying motive: the reason or urge that makes a customer buy.
Types: product motives (why this product) vs patronage motives (why from this seller); emotional (pride, fear, love, imitation, comfort) vs rational (economy, durability, safety, utility).
Primary (buy the product class) vs selective (buy a particular brand).
Application: identify the dominant motive early, stress the benefit that matches it, use it in the presentation and in handling objections and closing.
topics.frame: Meaning → types in a chart with an example each → how a salesperson uses them → conclusion.

topics.name: Buyer Behaviour
topics.summary: Buyer vs consumer, factors affecting buyer behaviour, why understanding it matters.
points: Buyer: the person who purchases; consumer: the person who uses (a parent buys toys, the child uses them).

Factors: cultural (culture, sub-culture, social class), social (family, reference groups, roles), personal (age, occupation, income, lifestyle, personality), psychological (motivation, perception, learning, beliefs and attitudes).
Why it matters for a salesperson: identify needs, choose the right approach, predict objections, build long-term relationships, increase sales.
topics.frame: Meaning → four factor groups as headings with examples → importance → conclusion.

topics.name: Selling Process, Prospecting & Qualifying
topics.summary: Steps of the personal selling process; prospecting vs qualifying; types of prospects.
points: Selling process: prospecting and qualifying → pre-approach → approach → presentation and demonstration → handling objections → closing → follow-up.
Prospecting: finding potential customers. Qualifying: checking they have need, ability to pay (money), authority to buy and are approachable (MAN — money, authority, need).
Prospecting methods: endless chain (referrals), centres of influence, cold calling, direct mail and e-mail, trade shows, internet and social media, company records, observation.
Prospect categories: hot (ready to buy), warm (interested), cold (unaware) — strategy for each: close quickly, nurture, educate.
The most crucial step is often identifying needs/pre-approach — a well-researched approach makes the rest easier (any step can be argued with reasons).
topics.frame: Meaning → flow chart of steps → one line and one example per step → conclusion.

topics.name: Salesmanship & Qualities of a Salesperson
topics.summary: Types of salesmanship, creative selling, role, qualities, duties and skills of a (modern) salesperson; careers.
points: Salesmanship: the art of persuading people to buy goods or services that satisfy their needs.
Types: creative (creating new demand), competitive (winning customers from rivals), service (after-sales support); also industrial, retail, wholesale.
Creative salesmanship process: identify prospects → understand needs → create desire → convince → close → follow-up.
Role of a modern salesperson: problem solver and consultant, relationship builder, source of market information, brand ambassador.
Qualities: physical (appearance, health), mental (alertness, memory, imagination), social (courtesy, tact), character (honesty, loyalty), vocational (product and customer knowledge).
Skills: communication, interpersonal, listening, negotiation, organisational (time and territory management), technology use.
Duties: meet targets, call on customers, collect orders and payments, report, handle complaints.
Careers: sales executive, key account manager, territory/area manager, retail, B2B, e-commerce sales.
topics.frame: Definition → qualities or duties grouped under headings, with examples → conclusion.

topics.name: Sales Management & Salesforce
topics.summary: Meaning, importance and scope of sales management; salesforce management process; recruitment, selection, training.
points: Sales management: planning, organising, directing and controlling the sales force to achieve sales objectives.
Importance: achieves revenue, links company and customer, market feedback, efficient use of salespeople.

Scope: sales planning and forecasting, territory and quota setting, organising the sales department, recruitment and selection, training, compensation, motivation, supervision and control, evaluation.
Salesforce management process: planning → recruitment → selection → training → compensation → motivation → supervision → evaluation.
Recruitment sources: internal (promotion, transfer, referrals) and external (advertisements, campus, agencies, online portals).
Selection: application → screening → tests → interviews → reference check → medical → offer and induction.
Training methods: classroom, on-the-job, role-play, case studies, e-learning, field training with a senior.
Trends: CRM software, data analytics, digital and social selling, remote selling.
topics.frame: Definition → process as a flow chart → one line per step → conclusion.

topics.name: Personal Selling: Concept & Situations
topics.summary: Meaning, nature, characteristics and objectives of personal selling; selling situations; selling vs marketing.
points: Personal selling: face-to-face, two-way communication to persuade a prospect to buy.
Characteristics: personal contact, two-way, flexible, relationship-building, immediate feedback, costly per contact.
Objectives: build sales, win new customers, keep existing ones, provide information and service, gather market feedback.
When to use: high-value or technical products, few large buyers, products needing demonstration, B2B.
Selling situations: retail (counter) selling, door-to-door, industrial/B2B, missionary selling (e.g. medical representatives), trade selling, telemarketing, service selling.
Selling vs marketing: selling focuses on the seller's need to convert products into cash; marketing on satisfying customer needs.
topics.frame: Definition → characteristics as headed points → situations table with examples → conclusion.

topics.name: Closing the Sale
topics.summary: Closing techniques, trial close and closing cues.
points: Closing: getting the prospect's commitment to buy.
Closing cues (buying signals): questions about price, delivery, guarantee; handling the product closely; nodding; asking others' opinion.
Trial close: a question to test readiness ('Which colour would you prefer?').

Techniques: assumptive close, alternative-choice close, summary close, special-offer (urgency) close, standing-room-only close, minor-point close, trial order, direct request, balance-sheet (pros and cons) close.
After closing: thank the customer, confirm the order, follow up to build repeat business.
topics.frame: Meaning → techniques as headed points each with a one-line example dialogue → conclusion.

topics.name: Ethics in Selling
topics.summary: Ethical and legal issues in selling, importance of ethics, sales code of conduct.
points: Ethics: moral principles of right and wrong in selling.
Ethical issues with customers: misrepresentation, high-pressure selling, bribes and gifts, favouritism, confidentiality.
With the employer: fudging expense accounts, misuse of company assets, moonlighting, misreporting calls.
With competitors: false statements about rivals, tampering with their products or displays.
Legal issues: Consumer Protection Act (unfair trade practices), Sale of Goods Act, contract law, misleading advertisements.
Importance: trust, long-term relationships, company reputation, avoiding legal action.
Code of conduct: honesty, transparency on price and terms, respect for customers' time and privacy, fair competition.
topics.frame: Meaning → issues grouped by stakeholder with examples → legal angle → conclusion.
